Messages.Body:
e Code Control (tww...@cs.usask.ca) writes:
> Some questions that have occured during game play. Any help
> would be appreciated...
>
> 1) If you attempt to diablarize a Vampire who has had the
> Bloodhunt card played on him, do you do so at +1 Stealth??

He can be attacked at +1 Stealth, granted, but what you're doing here is
the "Encounter Vampire in Torpor" action. Thus, you cannot use the +1
Stealth.

> 2) Can you use the Theft of Vitae card to steal two blood, then
> play the Taste of Vitae for two more blood? (In effect, stealing the
> same two points of blood twice?)

Stealing blood doesn't do damage, so you can't use taste of Vitae in this
case. This is also why those Steal Blood cards are really useful against
those ultra-Fortitude deck. You cannot prevent damage when there is no
damage, you know...:)

-Paul-Andre

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
tww...@cs.usask.ca (e Code Control) writes:

> Some questions that have occured during game play. Any help
>would be appreciated...

>1) If you attempt to diablarize a Vampire who has had the
>Bloodhunt card played on him, do you do so at +1 Stealth??

No diablerie is not "an attack" per se. You may not attack (via
Bum's Rush, Bloodhunt, nor Haven Uncovered) a vampire in torpor.

The only action you may take against a vampire in torpor is "Encounter
V in torpor to Diablerize", which is a (D) action at no stealth
(unless the target V is in your own torpor area, in which case the
action is undirected and (as usual for undirected actions) at +1 stealth).

Officially, that is.

>2) Can you use the Theft of Vitae card to steal two blood, then
>play the Taste of Vitae for two more blood? (In effect, stealing the
>same two points of blood twice?)

Officially, yes. The card says "Blood lost by opponent" without specifying
that it should've been lost to damage. So blood lost to stealing as well
as blood paid for combat cards (claws, Skin of steel, Blur, Blood fury)
all counts as "lost" blood.
--

Messages.Author: King Super Kool
Messages.Body:
Hi,

I have a few questions I'd like to ask, as I'm new to the game. Last night I
was playing with my wife and a friend and a few things arose.

1) I had Ebanezer Roush in play and his card states: Ebenezer may attack a
vampire of your predator or prey, providing that vampire's blood capacity in
no greater than 3. This is a +2 stealth (D) action. Ok, I wanted to attack a
tapped vampire with 2 blood capacity (and no blood). My friend swears up and
down you can't attack a tapped vampire. Is this true? I could not find any
reference to this in the rules.

2) Another question arose when I used Ebanezer to attack a vampire. My friend
(the same some as before) believed that attacking a players minion or any part
of his structure constitutes a Bleed and that he could play a card that can
only be played when he is being bled. The rules state the Bleeding is a
specific action, but he disagrees. Any thoughts?

3) This is one I'm not clear on. When you play a card that can be stolen or
destroyed by a directed action (D), do you need a specific card to perform the
(D) action? I played The Rack last night and my wife wanted to steal it from
me, but we were not sure how this goes. Help!

I'd really appreciate if somebody could help me on these questions. Thanks in
advanced!

Gary
ga...@ids.net

Messages.Author: Joseph W. Alfred
Messages.Body:
In article <GARY.39....@ids.net> GA...@ids.net (King Super Kool) writes:
>From: GA...@ids.net (King Super Kool)
>Subject: Rules Questions
>Date: Thu, 27 Jul 1995 12:10:28 +1000

>Hi,

> I have a few questions I'd like to ask, as I'm new to the game. Last night I
>was playing with my wife and a friend and a few things arose.

>1) I had Ebanezer Roush in play and his card states: Ebenezer may attack a
>vampire of your predator or prey, providing that vampire's blood capacity in
>no greater than 3. This is a +2 stealth (D) action. Ok, I wanted to attack a
>tapped vampire with 2 blood capacity (and no blood). My friend swears up and
>down you can't attack a tapped vampire. Is this true? I could not find any
>reference to this in the rules.

Ebanezer may attack a vampire of blood capacity 3 or less regardless of
whether the victim of the attack is tapped or not. Being attacked does not
tap the victim vampire if it is untapped.

>2) Another question arose when I used Ebanezer to attack a vampire. My friend
>(the same some as before) believed that attacking a players minion or any part
>of his structure constitutes a Bleed and that he could play a card that can
>only be played when he is being bled. The rules state the Bleeding is a
>specific action, but he disagrees. Any thoughts?

Your friend is completely and totally wrong. You are attacking a vampire, not
the methuselah, which is what a bleed is. Furthermore, you can normally
only bleed your prey, and Ebanezer allows you to attack a vampire of your
predator.

>3) This is one I'm not clear on. When you play a card that can be
stolen or >destroyed by a directed action (D), do you need a specific card to
perform the >(D) action? I played The Rack last night and my wife wanted to
steal it from >me, but we were not sure how this goes. Help!

It does not require a card to take any action specified on a location card.
If the action is a vote to burn the location, it typically is at +1 stealth,
but the acting vampire does not get the +1 vote that comes with playing a
political action card.

> I'd really appreciate if somebody could help me on these questions. Thanks in
>advanced!

>Gary
>ga...@ids.net

Have fun playing! It's a very addictive game, and the more people involved,
the better.

Messages.Author: Gary Schwartz
Messages.Body:
GA...@ids.net (King Super Kool) wrote:
>1) I had Ebanezer Roush in play and his card states: Ebenezer may attack a
>vampire of your predator or prey, providing that vampire's blood capacity in
>no greater than 3. This is a +2 stealth (D) action. Ok, I wanted to attack a
>tapped vampire with 2 blood capacity (and no blood). My friend swears up and
>down you can't attack a tapped vampire. Is this true? I could not find any
>reference to this in the rules.

Anything that allows you to attack a minion works even if the minion is
tapped, but attacking an untapped minion does not tap it.

>2) Another question arose when I used Ebanezer to attack a vampire. My friend
>(the same some as before) believed that attacking a players minion or any part
>of his structure constitutes a Bleed and that he could play a card that can
>only be played when he is being bled. The rules state the Bleeding is a
>specific action, but he disagrees. Any thoughts?

Your friend is full of it.

>3) This is one I'm not clear on. When you play a card that can be stolen or
>destroyed by a directed action (D), do you need a specific card to perform the
>(D) action? I played The Rack last night and my wife wanted to steal it from
>me, but we were not sure how this goes. Help!

All your wife had to do is say "I'm tapping Gilbert to steal the Rack."
Same goes for any cards destroyed by actions. For cards destroyed by political
actions, just tap to call a vote.

Hope this helps,
Gary

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
GA...@ids.net (King Super Kool) writes:

>1) I had Ebanezer Roush in play and his card states: Ebenezer may attack a
>vampire of your predator or prey, providing that vampire's blood capacity in
>no greater than 3. This is a +2 stealth (D) action. Ok, I wanted to attack a
>tapped vampire with 2 blood capacity (and no blood). My friend swears up and
>down you can't attack a tapped vampire. Is this true? I could not find any
>reference to this in the rules.

You may attack a tapped vampire.
Also, if you attack an untapped vampire, the target vampire is not tapped.

Combat has nothing to do with tapping. Ever.

>2) Another question arose when I used Ebanezer to attack a vampire. My friend
>(the same some as before) believed that attacking a players minion or any part
>of his structure constitutes a Bleed and that he could play a card that can
>only be played when he is being bled. The rules state the Bleeding is a
>specific action, but he disagrees. Any thoughts?

Bleed is Bleed. Nothing else is (attacking, calling a vote, etc. don't count)

>3) This is one I'm not clear on. When you play a card that can be stolen or
>destroyed by a directed action (D), do you need a specific card to perform the
>(D) action? I played The Rack last night and my wife wanted to steal it from
>me, but we were not sure how this goes. Help!

No. The card in play simply grants an added action option to all minions
as described on the card. You need no special card to take the described
action.
